title: Rogue Black Holes
subtitle: Invisible wanderers

description:
Episode 103 of a daily journey through the universe. 🕳️
We hunt rogue black holes: maybe 100 million drifting through the Milky Way, invisible, and the first one ever caught, OGLE-2011-BLG-0462, about 5,000 light-years away and about 7 times the Sun's mass, found by how it bent a star's light.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 104: Next stop, the day Earth's compass flips.

segments.text: Episode one hundred and three. Next stop... rogue black holes.
When the biggest stars die, many collapse into black holes. Some of them get kicked away, and drift alone.
segments.headline: Kicked out, drifting alone

segments.text: Scientists estimate there may be about one hundred million black holes in our galaxy. Most of them invisible.
A lone black hole gives off no light. So how do you find one?
segments.headline: How do you see it?

segments.text: You wait for it to pass in front of a distant star. Its gravity bends that star's light like a lens, and the star gets brighter.
segments.headline: Gravity bends light

segments.text: In twenty eleven, telescopes saw a star brighten for almost three hundred days. Hubble watched it for years.
segments.headline: Hubble keeps watching

segments.text: In twenty twenty-two, astronomers announced the first rogue black hole ever found. About five thousand light-years away.
A twenty twenty-five update weighed it: about seven times the mass of the Sun, moving fast through space.

segments.text: Don't worry. The nearest ones are still far, far away from us.
segments.headline: We're safe

segments.text: Tomorrow, we come home, to a planet whose magnetic north and south have swapped places hundreds of times. Follow, so you don't miss episode one hundred and four.
